doubts.verdict: Yes, it is a resonator bus in the strong sense. The transmons couple to one central computational resonator that can hold a qubit state (the MOVE operation), which gives effective all-to-all connectivity. That justifies the G-bus gap and a new cx_busres station. 'IQM Star' is the topology. 'IQM Star 24' is a QPU product (a device, not just a chip), offered on IQM Resonance. VLQ at IT4I is an on-premises installation of the same 24-qubit design. The row date '2024' fits only the 6-qubit star QPU; the first 24-qubit Star was delivered as VLQ. Halocene is an IQM Crystal (square-lattice) QPU and should be removed from the G-bus machine list.

doubts.verdict: Multi-level reset: yes. Willow resets its measure qubits with multi-level reset every cycle, and DQLR removes leakage from data qubits, so add ro_reset beside the G-lru gap. AlphaQubit 2 was fine-tuned and tested on Willow data for surface codes d=3/5/7 only. Its 'first real-time colour-code decoding at d=9' is throughput on TPU accelerators with simulated data, not decoding in Willow's control loop. doubts.verdict: Not a mid-circuit erasure check, so ro_img is right and ro_erasure is not. In the Nov-2024 logical runs with Microsoft, loss came from a separate 'survival' image taken after the circuit and was decoded as erasure. In the Jun-2026 toric-code work, the non-destructive state-selective image used for each mid-circuit measurement also flags loss ('delayed erasure conversion'). Ancillas are checked every cycle; data qubits only when they are measured. Missing atoms are refilled from a storage zone, and loss-aware PyMatching decoding runs offline. No ancilla-based check detects a lost data qubit during the code.

doubts.verdict: There were qubits at both ends, but the result is not between modules. IBM told EE Times (19 Aug 2026) that it had 'demonstrated a two-qubit operation across an L-coupler with 99.3% fidelity' (target 99.9%). A two-qubit operation needs a qubit at each end of the coupler, but IBM did not name the test hardware. The two cryogenic modules linked that month 'contained no processors' and were tested with an applied heat load; Nighthawk processors go in later in 2026. Module-to-module entanglement remains Cockatoo's 2027 target, so describe the 99.3% as a coupler result, not a module link.
